results.title: FAQ — Woomool
results.content:
## What is Woomool?

Woomool is an extended mind for visionaries: people who carry a lot of ideas and plans for a long time, and need to share them with the people they build with.

You talk or type, and Woomool’s AI agent turns your thinking into a graph on a shared canvas. Each idea becomes its own small node, connected to the ideas around it. You can take in the shape of your whole thinking at a glance, and the graph is still there the next time you pick it up.

## How is Woomool different from Obsidian?

Obsidian is built around documents. You write notes and link them together, and the graph view draws each note as a dot and each link as a line. [...] That graph tells you which notes are related, but not what they say. To follow your own thinking, you still have to open each note and read it.

Woomool is built around the graph itself. It breaks your thinking into small, separate ideas, and each one sits on the canvas as a node you can read. When you look at a Woomool graph, you see the thoughts themselves and how they fit together. The graph is the thinking, not a map of where it’s stored.

Woomool also has a voice AI agent built in. Think out loud, and the agent adds and connects ideas on the canvas as you speak. Obsidian doesn’t offer anything like that out of the box.

## How is Woomool different from Notion?

Notion is great for organizing work that has already taken shape: docs, wikis, databases, and project plans. [...] Woomool is for the step before that, while ideas are still forming. Instead of forcing early thoughts into pages and tables, you lay them out as connected nodes on a canvas, where the whole picture stays visible without clicking through nested pages.

Woomool is where you figure it out. Notion is where you write it down.

## How is Woomool different from Granola?

Granola helps after the meeting. It listens in, then gives you tidy notes and a summary once the call ends. Those notes are personal by default. You can share them, but they’re your record of what happened.

## No object cap. No time limit. [...] ## What is a visual thinking tool, and why work this way?

Visual thinking is working out ideas in space instead of in a straight line of text. Storyflow is an AI visual workspace that holds your visual thinking on one infinite canvas: mind maps, boards of cards, moodboards and diagrams side by side, with AI to lay out a starting board. Some people simply think better when they can see the whole shape of a problem at once: what connects to what, which parts cluster together, where the gap is. A visual thinking tool gives that mind a surface to spread out on, so the thinking becomes something you can point at rather than something you hold in your head. [...] Because it is a canvas and not a diagram, the thinking never dead-ends. Ask the AI to lay out a first board from a prompt, expand a cluster that feels thin, or attach a video reference next to an idea. Then turn the strongest part into a storyboard, a content calendar, or a project plan on the same canvas. The visual you made becomes the start of the work instead of a picture you screenshot and forget.

results.title: Introducing Canvas AI: a spatial agent for your canvas
results.content:
Moving things works the same way. To add a card, the agent picks something already on the board and says where the new card should go in relation to that item, for example underneath and lined up on the left. Causal then works out the exact position on screen.

We also taught the agent workflows for the things people ask for most. Ask for a roadmap and the agent sets out each stage in a sequential flow, with arrows joining each stage to the next. Ask for a mind map and the agent puts the main idea at the centre, with related ideas branching outward.

## Get Started on Your Canvas

Spatial reasoning in AI is a brand-new frontier, and Causal is built to be the shared workspace where you and artificial intelligence collaborate on the same surface. [...] ## How to Plan a Project with Canvas AI

With the integration of an AI assistant, the possibilities of creation are truly endless. These are only but a few ways we are actively using the agent to enhance our workflow:

## Collaboration

Think of the Spatial Agent as a teammate at the whiteboard with you. You bring the ideas, it helps shape them, and you both work on the same board at the same time. Teams use it as an AI whiteboard to map out product architecture, and as a Miro AI alternative for planning roadmaps that run over several weeks. [...] ## Bring Your Own Agent (MCP)

We believe you shouldn’t be locked into a single model or ecosystem. Alongside the Spatial Agent, we’re announcing support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Now you can bring your own agent directly to Causal. Whether you are running proprietary models, open-source LLMs, or specialized fine-tuned agents, MCP gives your AI full access to Causal’s spatial tools and visual creation language.

## How Does Spatial Reasoning in AI Actually Work?

Building the agent meant rethinking how an AI works with a canvas.

The agent never sees coordinates. The agent understands a board through relative positioning. When the agent looks at your board, Causal tells the agent which items are clustered together and how each group relates to the rest.
